C004.subject: AGI achievement within 20 years
C004.object: physical embodiment with fine-grained sensorimotor control for causal reasoning
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: AGI achievement within 20 years physical embodiment with fine-grained sensorimotor control for causal reasoning]

[PATH:empirical] Comparative studies of disembodied large language models vs. embodied agents (e.g., robotic manipulation with tactile sensors) on causal reasoning benchmarks (e.g., the 'BIRD' or 'CausalWorld' tasks). — Directly tests whether fine-grained sensorimotor control is necessary for causal reasoning by comparing performance of models with and without embodiment, controlling for other factors.

[PATH:literature] Longitudinal analysis of progress in AI-driven robotics (e.g., DARPA RoboChallenge, OpenAI Dactyl, or Google RT-2) tracking the correlation between advances in sensorimotor control and emergence of causal inference capabilities. — Provides historical and trend evidence on whether sensorimotor control has been a prerequisite for causal reasoning breakthroughs, helping to assess the likelihood of AGI requiring embodiment within 20 years.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical work on the 'symbol grounding problem' and 'causal learning from interventions' (e.g., using Pearl's causal hierarchy) to analyze whether abstract reasoning can be achieved without embodied interaction. — Formal analysis can clarify whether causal reasoning inherently requires physical intervention and feedback loops, or if it can be learned from passive data, thus refuting or supporting the hypothesis.

[PATH:empirical] Comparative performance analysis of embodied vs. non-embodied large language models on real-world task benchmarks (e.g., robot manipulation, navigation) over the next 5-10 years — Directly tests whether physical interaction learning is necessary for AGI-level competence in real-world domains, by tracking whether purely simulated or text-trained models can match embodied ones on tasks requiring physical understanding.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of causal learning and grounding requirements for general intelligence, drawing on cognitive science literature (e.g., embodied cognition, sensorimotor theory) and computational learning theory — Examines whether abstract symbolic reasoning can achieve sufficient world knowledge without physical interaction, or if embodiment provides essential inductive biases for causal structure learning, which would refute or support the hypothesis.

[PATH:literature] Longitudinal survey of AGI research roadmaps and historical progress in simulation-based learning (e.g., Minecraft, VirtualHome) versus robotic learning, with expert elicitation on milestones — Aggregates evidence from published research and expert forecasts to assess whether the field expects embodiment to be a bottleneck, providing a meta-level check on the hypothesis's plausibility over the 20-year window.

C006.subject: AGI achievement within 20 years
C006.object: physical embodiment for real-world interaction learning

[PATH:empirical] Comparative study of agent performance on common-sense physical reasoning tasks (e.g., stacking blocks, tool use) when trained in simulated environments with high-fidelity graphics vs. real-world physical robots with tactile and force feedback. — Directly tests whether physical embodiment and real-world interaction provide a measurable advantage over even the most realistic simulation for acquiring causal physical models.

[PATH:literature] Systematic literature review of transfer learning from simulation to reality (sim-to-real) in robotics, focusing on tasks requiring tactile and force feedback (e.g., peg-in-hole, deformable object manipulation). — Synthesizes existing evidence on whether simulation alone can ground the causal physical understanding needed for AGI, or if embodiment is essential despite perceptual realism.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of the necessity of sensorimotor contingency and active inference for learning causal models of physics, building on the 'symbol grounding problem' and 'embodied cognition' frameworks. — Provides a formal argument for or against the claim that tactile and proprioceptive feedback are necessary for grounding causal physical reasoning, independent of current empirical limitations.

scope.domain: acquisition of common sense physical reasoning through tactile and force feedback

qualifier.condition: even if simulation fidelity reaches human-level perceptual realism, because tactile and proprioceptive feedback are essential for grounding causal physical models

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of existing literature on sensorimotor grounding in cognitive science and developmental robotics (e.g., studies on affordance learning, active perception, and the role of embodiment in concept formation) — Synthesizes decades of evidence on whether real-world interaction is a prerequisite for general intelligence, providing theoretical grounding for or against the hypothesis.
